brief: Goldman added a 25bp September FOMC hike to its forecast last Friday after the August CPI report pushed market pricing to nearly 90 percent, arguing the Fed hikes not on strong fundamentals but because holding now risks a market reaction too negative to justify. GS expects a 10-8 dot majority for one 2026 hike, but sees risk of a two-hike majority if more participants read this week's move as a normal response to higher oil prices and AI demand. It expects the FOMC to avoid another hike in October given the midterms and limited new data, and to drop the case for further hikes by December as inflation improves and the tariff and Iran-war drivers fade. GS now sees two 2027 cuts landing in September and December (previously June and December) and raised its terminal rate forecast to 3.25-3.5 percent. Trading desks layer on color: rate vol is stressed with cheap 30-year convexity, FX favors USD shorts against JPY and AUD on a dovish outcome, equities flags a Fed hold (not a hike) as the bigger near-term risk, and gold has stayed range-bound despite an oil-supply shock from the Saudi pipeline attack.
